metadata.title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions
metadata.venue: ACM Trans. Multimedia Comput. Commun. Appl.

abstract: This work presents a multimodal text-keystrokes dataset and associated learning methods for emotion recognition. A dataset of 69 participants' text and keystroke data is collected, achieving 86.95% accuracy through feature fusion and outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in accuracy.

research.problem: Identifying dominant emotions from limited text data for human-computer interaction.
research.motivation: Enhance emotion recognition in computing systems using non-acted text and keystroke dynamics.
research.objective: Create a multimodal dataset and learning methods for accurate emotion detection from short text and keystrokes.

methodology.summary: Combines text and keystroke features from 69 participants' data using supervised learning and feature selection techniques.
methodology.training_strategy: Supervised learning with feature selection methods

experiments.experimental_setup: Data collected from 69 participants in controlled environments with video stimuli and unguided text reviews.
experiments.results: 86.95% accuracy via text-keystroke fusion; 100% accuracy for pleasure-displeasure classes using SVM with feature fusion.

contributions: Novel multimodal dataset combining text and keystrokes
Balanced labeled dataset for five basic emotions
limitations: Reliance on text and keystroke data
future_work: Expanding to other modalities like speech or EEG
analysis.research_gap: Lack of publicly available labeled datasets with comprehensive emotion classes.

sections.introduction: Discusses challenges in emotion recognition and motivation for multimodal data collection.
sections.related_work: References prior studies on affective computing and emotion detection methods.
sections.methodology: Details dataset collection, feature extraction, and learning framework design.
sections.results: Presents accuracy metrics and comparison with state-of-the-art techniques.
sections.discussion: Analyzes contributions, advantages, and limitations of the proposed approach.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes the work's impact on emotion recognition and future directions.
